Academic summary and critical response, essays, student lead discussions, and presentations were all based on articles on horror fiction. He did not make us read hundreds of pages for a single essay, we had 3 essays and a dictionary in total. We chose a horror scene of our liking for student-led discussions while other sections had to read articles for that. For essay 1 we chose 2 horror films from the list the instructor provided and compared them using 3 articles. We also read those articles in class and did activities on them so I did not have a hard time preparing for the essays. The topics he chose were easy to talk about, and he always tried to make the class entertaining for us. Not only he choose an engaging topic but he also taught us how to write an academic essay. He uploaded all materials in moodle and always sent us emails to remind us of important things (like if we were going to write an essay that week he would send an email reminding us of the materials we needed to bring and what we needed to do).  He would make sure the whole class was ready for anything we needed to do in an upcoming class. He would always set the assignment deadlines in consultation with the class and would rearrange them if he thought we wouldn't be ready. His comments and tutorials on essay 1 were also helpful. He also gave high marks on the assignments and did not use the spare hour unless he had to. The best ENG101 instructor you can find.

Linguistic courses should be designed in a way that assesses students' understanding of a language by any means possible, be it creative or formal. This course constricts students to a certain curriculum which tends to be quite suffocating because different students have different ways of expressing themselves. The fact that the only form of prose accepted in this course is argumentative essays tends to be troublesome for some students who have more of a creative mind and express themselves in a similar way. Language courses should assess students' understanding of a language as I previously mentioned, and some students who struggle with the essays in this course are extremely proficient in the english language but can not simply confine themselves to store their creative juices in the dingy four walls more commonly known as argumentative essays.

ENG 101 is a fun and relaxing course where you can learn different topics that vary a lot from many majors’ lessons if you have an excellent instructor. It also provides us an opportunity to meet and have lessons together from many different majors in our university. However, I feel like the course is too demanding and its workload is not always correlated to how much it affects the course’s overall grade. Assignments that take over a week’s worth of lessons only effect 5-6% of the grade, which I don’t think makes much sense.
